title: Writer table semantic preflight hardening

title: Writer table bookmark floating layer-order audit

title: Writer table bookmark floating layout render audit
acceptance: Render disposable DOCX fixtures with overlapping anchored images before and after WPS save; compare visible placement and stacking from exported page images, and reject layout changes that invalidate the audited drawing semantics.

A character-relative anchor demonstrably shifts with glyph width and is rejected before backup; its preflight regression passes.

title: Writer floating image wrap and edge clipping audit
acceptance: Real WPS clamps out-of-cell coordinates to the cell edge; with layoutInCell disabled, a negative page-relative anchor clips to a 144x108 raster region. None, square, and topAndBottom wrapping plus crop metadata retain drawing semantics and pixel masks through bookmark fill; adjacent After character bounds remain unchanged.

title: Writer floating image pagination and multi-paragraph flow audit
acceptance: A real-WPS multi-page table-cell bookmark fixture retains page count, PREFACE and AFTER-TABLE marker page/character bounds, drawing semantics, and pixel-identical full-page PDF rasters before and after fill.

title: Writer multi-anchor cross-page stacking and pagination audit
acceptance: Real WPS retains first-page red and later-page blue anchor visibility, relativeHeight ranking, marker page/character bounds, full-page raster images, and per-color masks through table-cell bookmark fill.

title: Writer tight and through wrap semantics and layout audit
acceptance: Diamond wrapPolygon paths with tight and through modes retain their DrawingML node/vertices, rendered page raster, extracted text, and table-bookmark fill read-back through real WPS save.

title: Writer wrap-side and floating distance audit
acceptance: Real WPS preserves left/right/largest wrapText, three asymmetric distT/distB/distL/distR combinations, long wrapped paragraph text, and full-page rasters through bookmark fill; drawing snapshots now expose all four distances.

title: Writer wrap geometry input preflight
acceptance: Preflight rejects tight/through wraps with missing polygon, fewer than two line points, out-of-range coordinates, and negative anchor distance before backup/WPS; disposable target bytes stay identical and all 12 WPS drawing integrations pass.

title: Writer concave wrap polygon and self-intersection audit
acceptance: Concave L-shaped tight/through paths retain DrawingML vertices, text, and WPS raster; self-intersecting and zero-area paths are rejected before backup with unchanged DOCX bytes; all 13 WPS drawing integrations pass.

title: Writer wrap polygon winding and closure audit
acceptance: Eight tight/through combinations of clockwise/counterclockwise and explicit/implicit closure pass real WPS bookmark fill; each input retains its own DrawingML, text, and PDF raster before/after. Explicit repeated-start closure renders differently from implicit closure and is documented as non-equivalent in WPS.

title: Writer wrap polygon vertex normalization audit
acceptance: Four cyclic start vertices of a concave outline in tight/through each pass real WPS round-trip; raw DrawingML sequence and each file's own raster remain stable. Different cyclic starts produce different PDF rasters, so vertex sequences must not be normalized by cyclic rotation.

title: Writer wrap polygon collinear vertices and rendering audit
acceptance: Adding collinear midpoints to a concave outline changes tight and through WPS rasters; both source variants independently retain their DrawingML, text, and raster through WPS save. Collinear vertices must not be simplified.

title: Writer wrap polygon near-degenerate and boundary audit
acceptance: Adjacent vertices one coordinate unit apart and valid points at 1/21599 near the polygon bounds pass offline preflight; four tight/through WPS round-trips retain DrawingML, text, and PDF rasters.

title: Writer wrap polygon near-collinear vertex audit
acceptance: A midpoint offset of 120/21600 renders pixel-identically to the collinear path at the current 1.5x PDF raster; each tight/through source retains exact vertices and its own raster through WPS save. Pixel equivalence is resolution-bound; preserve exact vertices.

title: Writer wrap polygon high-resolution raster audit
acceptance: At 4x PDF raster, straight, 120/21600-offset, and 600/21600-offset outlines produce identical page pixels in tight/through for this fixture; each exact DrawingML input and its WPS round-trip remain stable. This is fixture/path-specific and does not claim geometric semantic equivalence.

title: Writer wrap polygon coordinate lexical validation audit
acceptance: +10800 and whitespace/leading-zero integer lexemes normalize to the same numeric snapshot; both pass real WPS round-trip. Decimal and empty coordinates are rejected before backup/COM with unchanged DOCX bytes.

title: Writer wrap coordinate boundary and oversized integer audit
acceptance: Real WPS tight/through fixtures cover valid 0/21600 endpoints; a 200-digit coordinate integer is rejected before backup/WPS with unchanged target bytes.

title: Writer wrap coordinate ASCII lexical audit
acceptance: Coordinate preflight and snapshots share an ASCII XML integer parser; sign/leading-zero/XML-whitespace spellings normalize, while Unicode digits, decimals, empty strings, and 200-digit out-of-range values reject before backup/WPS with unchanged bytes.

title: Writer wrap coordinate XML whitespace boundary audit
acceptance: Tab/newline XML attribute whitespace folds to the same integer snapshot; NBSP is not accepted as XML integer whitespace and rejects before backup/WPS with unchanged bytes.

title: Writer wrap coordinate signed zero audit
acceptance: -0/+00 normalize to numeric zero; four signed/leading-zero/whitespace/signed-zero lexemes retain drawing semantics, text, and PDF raster through real WPS bookmark fill.

title: Writer wrap coordinate malformed sign audit
acceptance: ++21600, sign-only +, and embedded whitespace 21 600 are rejected as invalid coordinate lexemes before backup/WPS with unchanged target bytes.

title: Writer wrap coordinate negative and negative-zero boundary audit
acceptance: -1 is rejected before backup/WPS; -0 normalizes to zero and passes real WPS round-trip; 0/21600 endpoints are covered by tight/through WPS fixtures.

title: Writer wrap distance lexical and numeric audit
acceptance: Distance preflight/snapshots share the ASCII XML integer parser; sign/leading-zero/XML whitespace forms normalize and pass real WPS, while Unicode digits, decimals, empty, and negative values reject before backup.

title: Writer wrap distance integer range audit
acceptance: Distances require nonnegative 635-EMU/twip alignment and Word signed-32 range; 2147483640 round-trips through real WPS, while nonaligned, signed-32/UInt32 overflow, and 200-digit values reject before backup.

title: Writer wrap distance default normalization audit
acceptance: Normalize omitted distances to measured WPS defaults (top/bottom 0, left/right 114300 EMU); omitted and explicit zero cases for all five wrap types pass real-WPS semantic, text, and per-document raster round trips.

title: Writer one-sided wrap with default distances audit
acceptance: left/right/largest wrapText with all four distances omitted pass real-WPS bookmark fill; default distances, DrawingML snapshots, PDF text, and 1.5x raster remain stable.

title: Writer mixed explicit/default wrap distances audit
acceptance: Three mixed directional distance combinations pass real WPS; omitted sides use distT/B=0 and distL/R=114300 EMU while explicit 635/1270 EMU values remain unchanged, with stable semantics, text, and PDF raster.

title: Writer wrapText default audit

title: Writer polygon wrapText default audit
acceptance: tight/through omitted wrapText snapshots equal explicit bothSides; real-WPS bookmark fill preserves DrawingML, PDF text, and raster for both modes.

title: Writer top-and-bottom wrapText default WPS audit

acceptance: Update safe performance-baseline MCP smoke scenarios from the stale 47-tool minimum to the current 81-tool catalog so a partial tools/list surface fails the baseline; add focused tests proving both smoke and config audit use the expected count.

acceptance: Reject tools/list cursors longer than 128 characters before base64 decoding, return JSON-RPC -32602, and retain valid first/next/final-page behavior; add oversized-input regression coverage.

acceptance: Ensure mcp-smoke returns structured failed checks rather than raising when initialize, tools/list, or tools/call responses have missing, null, or malformed result structures; keep compact page summaries safe and test an error response with result=null.

title: Refresh local sync package after MCP pagination hardening
acceptance: Create a current local sync package after the pagination, cursor-bound, stdio, audit, smoke, and documentation updates; refresh safe regression evidence and verify package coverage/readiness, project status, and documentation freshness without remote Git requirements.

title: Reject blank MCP tool names in catalog audits
acceptance: Treat empty and whitespace-only tool names as invalid in both mcp-smoke and mcp-config-audit, preserve duplicate checks for valid names, and add tests proving an otherwise sufficient catalog with a blank name fails both audits.

title: Validate MCP tool naming recommendations
acceptance: Validate audited tool names against MCP's recommended 1-128 ASCII character set [A-Za-z0-9_.-] in both smoke and configured-client audit, count invalid and duplicate names independently, and test spaces, special characters, overlength, and valid boundary names.

title: Verify MCP stdio recovery after malformed requests
acceptance: Through a live mcp-server subprocess, send malformed JSON and valid non-object JSON requests, verify -32700/-32600 responses with null IDs, then initialize successfully on the same process and exit cleanly at EOF.

title: Harden MCP JSON-RPC request envelope validation
acceptance: Audit JSON-RPC request envelope types and IDs against the supported MCP stdio contract; add focused handler and subprocess tests for malformed versions, methods, IDs, and params while preserving process continuity and valid notifications.

title: Validate MCP initialize version negotiation
acceptance: Validate initialize params and supported protocol-version selection against the MCP lifecycle contract; preserve client request IDs, return a deterministic supported version or a protocol error as required, and cover matching, unsupported, malformed, and missing version cases through handler and stdio tests.

title: Enforce MCP initialize-before-operation lifecycle
acceptance: For persistent stdio sessions, require a successful initialize before normal requests and an initialized notification before operations; reject out-of-order calls without side effects, preserve process continuity, and verify valid ordering through subprocess tests while documenting the one-shot CLI exception if retained.

title: Reject ambiguous duplicate JSON object keys in MCP stdio
acceptance: Reject JSON lines containing duplicate object member names at any nesting level before dispatch, return a bounded parse/invalid-request error with null ID, and prove duplicate method/ID/tool argument inputs cannot cause side effects or break following valid requests.

title: Bound MCP stdio input line size
acceptance: Apply a documented maximum line length before JSON decoding, drain oversized records without buffering them in full, return one bounded invalid-request error, and continue processing the following valid line in the same process.

title: Reject non-standard JSON numeric constants in MCP stdio
acceptance: Reject NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity during MCP JSON decoding with a bounded parse error; ensure nested occurrences are rejected before dispatch and a following valid request succeeds in the same stdio session.

title: Enforce unique request IDs within MCP stdio sessions
acceptance: Track valid string/integer request IDs per persistent stdio session, reject reused IDs before dispatch with a bounded JSON-RPC error, and verify a duplicate mutating call has no side effect while a later unique request succeeds.

title: Align MCP output schemas with structured tool results
acceptance: Make every advertised outputSchema describe the actual tools/call structuredContent shape, then validate the catalog-wide schema contract and both successful and tool-error result envelopes against it.

title: Return protocol errors for unknown MCP tools
acceptance: Reject tools/call names absent from the live MCP catalog as JSON-RPC invalid-params errors before invoking the adapter; preserve normal tool execution failures as isError tool results and prove both paths through handler and stdio tests.

title: Validate MCP tool arguments against input schemas
acceptance: Validate provided arguments against catalog JSON Schema types, required/unknown fields, enum, numeric bounds, and array item types before adapter dispatch; return -32602 without side effects and keep known-tool execution failures as isError results.

title: Audit configured MCP clients over persistent stdio sessions
acceptance: Run initialize, initialized notification, and complete paginated tools/list traversal through one configured server process; verify response IDs, bounded deadlines, clean EOF exit, and preserve diagnostics without one-shot lifecycle bypass.

title: Implement the MCP ping utility request
acceptance: Support the legacy protocol ping request with an empty result, accept absent or empty params, reject nonempty params as invalid params, and verify the request works through persistent stdio after initialization.

title: Validate configured MCP tool descriptors and schemas
acceptance: During persistent configured-client audit, validate every tools/list descriptor has the expected MCP shape and usable input/output schemas; report malformed descriptors with bounded diagnostics and add paginated fake-server plus real configuration tests.

title: Bound configured MCP audit output buffering
acceptance: Limit stdout line size and queued response buffering while continuously draining stderr from configured MCP servers; oversized output fails with bounded diagnostics, process cleanup completes, and later normal persistent audits still pass.

title: Normalize malformed MCP audit responses
acceptance: Convert malformed JSON, excessive nesting, and invalid UTF-8 from configured MCP subprocesses into bounded audit failures without uncaught reader-thread exceptions; always reap the child and preserve subsequent independent audits.

title: Validate nested MCP descriptor schema definitions
acceptance: Recursively validate nested properties, array items, required fields, and JSON Schema keyword shapes in advertised MCP input/output schemas; report bounded page/index/schema-path diagnostics and preserve the real configured catalog audit.

title: Validate MCP initialize metadata in configured audit
acceptance: Require nonempty serverInfo name/version and validate capabilities/tools metadata shape during initialize; malformed handshakes produce bounded configured-audit failures, clean up the process, and do not block later valid audits.

title: Require negotiated tools capability before MCP audit traversal
acceptance: Require initialize to advertise the tools capability before tools/list traversal, reject missing capability as a bounded handshake failure, reap the process, and retain successful audits for valid servers.

title: Validate optional MCP implementation metadata
